---
title: "Annual Rating Activity Analysis"
author: "Dina Muhamaitihan"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(scales)
```

## 1. Load Data

```{r load}
# Adjust this path to where your MovieLens 32M files are
DATA_PATH <- "D:/桌面/ml-32m/"

# data.table is much faster than read.csv for large files
ratings <- fread(paste0(DATA_PATH, "ratings.csv"))

# Extract year from Unix timestamp
ratings[, date := as.POSIXct(timestamp, origin="1970-01-01")]
ratings[, year := as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))]

cat("Total ratings:", nrow(ratings), "\n")
cat("Year range:", min(ratings$year), "-", max(ratings$year), "\n")
```

## 2. Ratings and Users Per Year

```{r annual_stats}
annual <- ratings[, .(
  n_ratings = .N,
  n_users   = uniqueN(userId),
  avg_rating = round(mean(rating), 3)
), by = year][order(year)]

print(annual)
```

## 3. Visualise Activity Over Time

```{r plot_ratings, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
ggplot(annual, aes(x=year, y=n_ratings)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill="steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label=scales::comma(n_ratings)),
            vjust=-0.3, size=2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::comma) +
  labs(title="Number of Ratings by Year (MovieLens 32M)",
       x="Year", y="Number of Ratings") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r plot_users, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
ggplot(annual, aes(x=year, y=n_users)) +
  geom_line(color="coral", linewidth=1) +
  geom_point(color="coral", size=2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::comma) +
  labs(title="Number of Active Users by Year (MovieLens 32M)",
       x="Year", y="Number of Users") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r plot_avg_rating, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
# Does average rating drift over time? This is evidence for temporal dynamics
ggplot(annual, aes(x=year, y=avg_rating)) +
  geom_line(color="purple", linewidth=1) +
  geom_point(color="purple", size=2) +
  ylim(3, 4.5) +
  labs(title="Average Rating by Year — Evidence for Temporal Dynamics",
       x="Year", y="Average Rating") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 4. Identify Most Active Period

```{r active_period}
# Find top years by rating volume
top_years <- annual[order(-n_ratings)][1:10]
cat("Top 10 most active years:\n")
print(top_years)

# Find years with > 1 million ratings
active_years <- annual[n_ratings > 1e6]
cat("\nYears with more than 1 million ratings:\n")
print(active_years)
```

## 5. Data Selection Rationale

```{r rationale}
# Observation 1: suspicious spike in 1996 (25,000 users) —
#   likely a batch import artifact; early data is unreliable
# Observation 2: most stable high-activity period is 2015-2019,
#   with 1.3M-1.9M ratings and 8k-16k active users per year
# Observation 3: average rating drifts over time (3.44 to 3.75),
#   justifying temporal dynamics modelling
# Observation 4: 2020 shows a COVID effect (increased activity),
#   making it an interesting and realistic test year

cat("Key observations:\n")
cat("  1996 user spike:", comma(annual[year == 1996, n_users]),
    "users — likely artifact, early data excluded\n")
cat("  2000 ratings peak:", comma(annual[year == 2000, n_ratings]), "\n")
cat("  2015 ratings peak:", comma(annual[year == 2015, n_ratings]), "\n")
cat("  Average rating range:",
    min(annual$avg_rating), "-", max(annual$avg_rating), "\n")
```

## 6. Proposed Train / Test Split

```{r split}
# Strategy: train on the most active and stable consecutive years,
# hold out the following year as the test set.
# This simulates realistic temporal prediction —
# using past behaviour to recommend for the future.

train <- ratings[year >= TRAIN_START & year <= TRAIN_END]
test  <- ratings[year == TEST_YEAR]

cat("=== Selected Train / Test Split ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Training : %d-%d | %s ratings | %s users\n",
    TRAIN_START, TRAIN_END,
    comma(nrow(train)),
    comma(uniqueN(train$userId))))
cat(sprintf("Test     : %d      | %s ratings | %s users\n",
    TEST_YEAR,
    comma(nrow(test)),
    comma(uniqueN(test$userId))))
```
